# Research Findings: Influenza Vaccination and Alzheimer's Disease

**Conclusion: The claim is false. The evidence points the opposite direction — flu vaccination is associated with a *reduced* risk of Alzheimer's disease, not an increased one.**

## What the evidence shows

Multiple peer-reviewed studies consistently find flu vaccination is associated with *lower* Alzheimer's risk, not higher:

- A large claims-based cohort study using propensity score matching found flu vaccination was linked to a **40% reduction** in Alzheimer's disease risk among older adults over a four-year period ([neurosciencenews.com](https://neurosciencenews.com/flu-vaccination-alzheimers-20909/)).
- Research presented at the Alzheimer's Association International Conference similarly found flu and pneumonia vaccinations tied to lower dementia risk ([aaic.alz.org](https://aaic.alz.org/releases_2020/vaccines-dementia-risk.asp)).
- A large study covered by the New York Times (June 2025) reinforces that vaccines including flu shots appear protective against dementia in older adults, while noting real adverse effects (like rare Guillain-Barré syndrome) are minor and don't outweigh benefits ([nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/14/health/elderly-vaccines-dementia.html)).
- Fact-checking organizations have specifically debunked related vaccine-Alzheimer's causation claims (mostly concerning COVID-19 vaccines), finding the underlying studies scientifically unsound, published in non-rigorous journals, or authored by individuals with a history of anti-vaccine advocacy ([politifact.com](https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2021/feb/26/j-bart-classen/coronavirus-vaccine-doesnt-cause-alzheimers-als/)).

## Caveats

Nearly all supportive studies are observational (cohort/claims-based), not randomized trials, so they cannot fully rule out confounding — but they support a *protective* association, not a harmful one. No credible study in this evidence set supports flu vaccination causing Alzheimer's.

## Bottom line

The scientific consensus in the reviewed sources contradicts the claim. If anything, evidence suggests flu vaccination may lower Alzheimer's risk.
